metadata.summary: Nico Rosberg believes George Russell will currently be driven by a similar level of "insane motivation" to turn the tables on Kimi Antonelli as he was to get the better of Lewis Hamilton after recurring defeats.
metadata.content: George Russell: Mercedes driver's losses to Kimi Antonelli will feel 'painful' says Nico Rosberg as driver backed for breakthrough | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content George Russell: Mercedes driver's losses to Kimi Antonelli will feel 'painful' says Nico Rosberg as driver backed for breakthrough George Russell fell 81 points behind Kimi Antonelli at the Madring; Russell conceded that "realistically I'm not in the fight for the drivers'" after the race; watch every session of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from September 24-26 with a Saturday race, live on Sky Sports F1 Tuesday 15 September 2026 14:14, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell on how the Virtual Safety Car compromised his race at the Spanish Grand Prix Nico Rosberg believes George Russell will currently be driven by a similar level of "insane motivation" to turn the tables on Kimi Antonelli as he was to get the better of Lewis Hamilton after recurring defeats. Russell's hopes of becoming world champion for the first time this year are increasingly slim with in-form Mercedes team-mate Antonelli opening an 81-point lead over him at the top of the standings. Since winning March's season-opening Australian Grand Prix, pre-season title favourite Russell has only twice finished ahead of Antonelli in the last 10 races they have both completed with the Briton seeing the young Italian take his seventh and eighth wins of the season across the Monza-Madrid double header. messages.text: London misses out as Nairobi secures 2029 World Athletics Championships

metadata.summary: The World Athletics Championships are heading to Africa for the first time after Kenya's capital Nairobi was confirmed as host of the 2029 edition, with London missing out.
metadata.content: World Athletics Championships: London misses out as Nairobi secures 2029 event | 'We are deeply disappointed' | Sky Sports Skip to content World Athletics Championships: London misses out as Nairobi secures 2029 event | 'We are deeply disappointed' The 2029 World Athletics Championships will be held in Nairobi, Kenya; it will be the first time the event has taken place in Africa; London's bid was unsuccessful, with UK Athletics CEO Jack Buckner saying: "We had an outstanding bid which would genuinely take the sport to new levels" Tuesday 15 September 2026 15:56, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player World Athletics President Lord Coe explains why they have awarded the World Championships to Nairobi and Munich with London missing out. The World Athletics Championships are heading to Africa for the first time after Kenya's capital Nairobi was confirmed as host of the 2029 edition, with London missing out. Kenya has long been a superpower in distance running but has yet to host an event of this scale. The championships will return to Germany in 2031 with Munich hosting. "We were fortunate to have four outstanding bids for 2029 and 2031, and this was not an easy decision for the council," said World Athletics president Sebastian Coe as he announced the decision following the Ultimate Championship in Hungary.
